{{Short description|British chemist (1941–2020)}}
{{use dmy dates|date=May 2021}}

'''Julian Philip Perry Robinson''' (11 November 1941 – 22 April 2020)<ref>{{cite news |title=Julian Perry Robinson, top chemical and biological arms control expert, dies of coronavirus |website=Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists |url=https://thebulletin.org/2020/04/julian-perry-robinson-top-chemical-and-biological-arms-control-expert-dies-of-coronavirus/ |access-date=1 May 2020 |date=30 April 2020}}</ref> was a British [[chemist]] and [[peace research]]er.<ref name=middlebury-in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020>{{Cite web |last=Hart |first=John |title=In Memoriam—Professor Julian Perry Robinson (1941–2020) |publisher=[[Middlebury Institute of International Studies at Monterey]] |url=https://www.nonproliferation.org/in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020/ |date=24 April 2020 |access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref><ref name=sipri-former-sipri-researcher-julian-perry-robinson-memoriam />

==Early life==
Born in [[Jerusalem]], Perry Robinson was educated at [[Canford School]], and went to [[Merton College, Oxford]] in 1960 to study Chemistry; he took a second class degree in 1964.<ref name="MCreg">{{cite book |title=Merton College Register 1900-1964 |editor-last=Levens |editor-first=R.G.C. |year=1964 |publisher=Basil Blackwell |location=Oxford |page=525}}</ref><ref name="TimesObit">{{cite news |title=Professor Julian Perry Robinson obituary |newspaper=[[The Times]] |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/professor-julian-perry-robinson-obituary-5d7gtgg9j |access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref> After university he spent four years studying national and international patent law with a London-based firm of Chartered Patent Agents.<ref name="GuardianObit">{{cite news |last=Guthrie |first=Richard |title=Julian Perry Robinson obituary |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/may/08/julian-perry-robinson-obituary |access-date=21 January 2021 |date=8 May 2020}}</ref><ref name="Nature">{{cite journal |last=McLeish |first=Caitriona |title=Julian Perry Robinson (1941–2020) |journal=Nature |date=28 May 2020 |volume=581 |issue=7809 |page=378 |doi=10.1038/d41586-020-01450-1 |bibcode=2020Natur.581..378M |s2cid=218772190 |url=https://media.nature.com/original/magazine-assets/d41586-020-01450-1/d41586-020-01450-1.pdf}}</ref>

==Career==
Robinson held research appointments at the [[Free University of Berlin]], [[Harvard University]] and the [[University of Sussex]].<ref name=middlebury-in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020 />

Robinson was a consultant to the [[World Health Organization]], [[United Nations]], the [[International Committee of the Red Cross]] and the [[United Nations Environment Programme]].<ref name=middlebury-in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020 />

Robinson was a member of staff at the [[Stockholm International Peace Research Institute]] from 1968 to 1971.<ref name=middlebury-in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020 /> While there he was a principal contributor to the six volume study ''The Problem of Chemical and Biological Warfare''.<ref name=middlebury-in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020 />

Robinson was also a co-convenor of the Pugwash Study Group on Implementation of the Chemical and Biological Weapons Conventions, co-directed the [[Science Policy Research Unit|Harvard Sussex Program]] on Chemical and Biological Weapons, which published the ''CBW Conventions Bulletin''.<ref name=middlebury-in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020 />

==Personal life and death==
Robinson died on 22 April 2020 as a result of complications related to [[COVID-19]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in England]].<ref name=middlebury-in-memoriam-professor-julian-perry-robinson-1941-2020 /><ref name=sipri-former-sipri-researcher-julian-perry-robinson-memoriam>{{Cite web |title=Former SIPRI Researcher Julian Perry Robinson—in memoriam |publisher=[[Stockholm International Peace Research Institute]] |url=https://sipri.org/media/2020/former-sipri-researcher-julian-perry-robinson-memoriam |date=24 April 2020 |access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> His widow is the academic [[Mary Kaldor]].
